description.p: boot.R is a small boot manager for UEFI computers. At power-on it scans your drives for installed operating systems and shows them as large, labelled tiles you can pick with the arrow keys, then starts the one you choose.
You can set a default system and an auto-boot countdown, rename, hide and reorder entries, and jump to the firmware setup screen. It is a single self-contained file with no dependencies.

This package installs the boot manager files and a command, boot-r-install, that copies boot.R to your EFI System Partition and adds it as the first boot entry. Nothing on your system is changed until you run that command. The app is unsigned, so Secure Boot must be turned off.

Adds mouse and trackpad support, including Synaptics I2C trackpads (tap to click and two-finger scroll), and a scroll bar in Settings. Text and distro logos are sharper on 4K and high-DPI screens, and booting a system no longer shows the splash screen first.
Fixes a kernel panic when booting an EFI-stub kernel such as Pop!_OS: boot.R now passes the kernel command line and initramfs from the system's boot entries.
Finds EFI-stub kernels (such as Pop!_OS via kernelstub) that have no separate loader file, and uses the display's native resolution on 4K and 5K screens. Adds a one-step Flatpak install script.
Adds a self-hosted Flatpak that runs the installer on the host.
